verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic was a British passenger liner.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'British-registered ship in the White Star line'; R3: 'White Star Line steamship carrying the British flag'; R5: 'British registered ship of the White Star Line'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm it was a British-registered passenger liner of White Star Line.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic sank on April 15, 1912.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On April 15, 1912... Titanic broke apart and sank'; R3: 'At 2:20 a.m. she sank'; R4: 'sank... on April 15'; R5: 'On April 15, 1912... sank'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'smashed into an iceberg in the north Atlantic'; R5: 'sank to the bottom of the North Atlantic Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in sources.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic sank after striking an iceberg.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after striking an iceberg, Titanic broke apart and sank'; R5: 'after striking an iceberg, Titanic broke apart and sank'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm sinking followed iceberg strike.

verifications.claim: Over 1,500 of the 2,200+ passengers and crew on board the RMS Titanic died.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '2,240 passengers and crew... more than 1,500 passengers and crew'; R3: '2,227 passengers and crew... Lost at sea were 1,522'; R6: 'more than 2,200 passengers and crew... over 1500 lives were lost'
verifications.reasoning: Numbers match closely across sources.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic was the world's largest luxury ship at the time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'largest and most luxurious passenger ship of its time'; R5: 'largest and most luxurious passenger ship of its time'; R6: 'largest ever movable man-made object'
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as largest and luxurious.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic weighed approximately 52,310 long tons.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'displacing (or weighing) 52,310 long tons'
verifications.reasoning: Exact figure and term 'weighing' used.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic was on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City when the disaster occurred.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'maiden voyage from Southampton on April 10, 1912... to New York City'; R3: 'maiden voyage from Southampton, England, to New York'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm route and maiden voyage status.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic struck an iceberg at 11:40 p.m. on April 14, 1912.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'At 11:40 p.m. on the night of 14 April... struck an iceberg'; R6: 'At 11:40 p.m.... spotted an iceberg'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and date directly stated.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic sank at 2:20 a.m. on April 15, 1912.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'At 2:20 a.m. she sank'; R4: 'Titanic finally went under at 2:20 a.m. April 15'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and date confirmed.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic collided with an iceberg.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'striking an iceberg'; R4: 'smashed into an iceberg'
verifications.reasoning: 'Collided' synonymous with 'struck' in sources.

verifications.claim: The iceberg collision damaged the RMS Titanic hull.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'iceberg had a jagged underwater spur, which slashed long gashes in the hull below the ship’s waterline'
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of hull damage from collision.

verifications.claim: The iceberg collision broke apart the RMS Titanic.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after striking an iceberg, Titanic broke apart and sank'; R5: 'after striking an iceberg, Titanic broke apart'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state it broke apart after iceberg strike.

verifications.claim: Approximately 705 to 710 people survived the RMS Titanic sinking.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The 705 survivors'; R4: '712 survivors'
verifications.reasoning: Sources cite 705 and 712, matching approximate range.

verifications.claim: Over 1,500 people perished in the RMS Titanic sinking.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'more than 1,500 passengers and crew'; R3: '1,522 people'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent across sources.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic had a displacement of 52,310 long tons.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'displacing... 52,310 long tons'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for displacement attributed to Titanic.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic was 883 feet long.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '883-foot Titanic'; R6: '883 feet long'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated, minor variation to 882.5 in R3 but primarily 883.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic maiden voyage was from Southampton, England, to New York City.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'maiden voyage from Southampton... New York City'; R3: 'maiden voyage from Southampton, England, to New York'
verifications.reasoning: Exact route confirmed.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic maiden voyage had planned stops in Cherbourg, France.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'stopped in Cherbourg, France, to pick up additional passengers'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as a stop.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic maiden voyage had planned stops in Queenstown (now Cobh), Ireland.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'sailed for Queenstown, Ireland'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as a stop.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic wreckage lies 12,000 feet below sea level.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '12,000 feet below sea level'; R5: '12,000 feet below sea level'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in multiple sources, despite R3's 12,500 ft variation.

verifications.claim: The RMS Titanic wreckage is roughly 350 nautical miles off the coast of Newfoundland, Canada.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'over 350 nautical miles off the coast of Newfoundland, Canada'; R3: 'about 350 miles... southeast of Newfoundland'
verifications.reasoning: 'Roughly' matches 'over/approximately 350'.

verifications.claim: The 1997 film Titanic was directed by James Cameron.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'James Cameron megahit Titanic'; R2: 'James Cameron's 'Titanic''
verifications.reasoning: Direct attribution of direction to James Cameron for 1997 film.
